chapter: Ch 4: Presentation and Disclosures Based Accounting Standards
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction, Objective & Scope of AS 17
explain: AS 17 is mandatory for Non-SMCs and Level 1 non-corporate entities.
It sets rules for reporting financial data by business lines and geographical areas.
Helps users better assess risks, returns, and overall performance of diversified entities.
If both consolidated and separate parent financial statements are presented, segment info is required only for consolidated statements.

flow.title: Steps in Segment Reporting
steps: Identify Business or Geographical Segments
Apply Tests for Reportable Segments
Prepare Segmental Report with Disclosures

topics.example: A company selling electronics and operating in India and UK presents segment reporting in its consolidated statements.
remember: Mandatory for Non-SMCs and Level 1 non-corporates.
Segment reporting is presented only on Consolidated Financial Statements when parent statements are attached.
mistakes: Disclosing segment information separately for parent statements when consolidated statements are already present.

quiz.q: For which entities is AS 17 mandatory?
quiz.why: AS 17 is mandatory for non-SMCs and Level 1 non-corporate entities.

quiz.q: Where must segment information be presented if both separate and consolidated statements are published?
o: On both separate and consolidated statements
quiz.why: AS 17 requires segment information to be presented only on the basis of consolidated financial statements.

topics.title: Definition of Business and Geographical Segments
explain: A Business Segment is a component producing related products/services with distinct risks and returns.
Factors for business segments include nature of products, production processes, customer types, and distribution methods.
A Geographical Segment operates in a specific economic environment with unique risks and returns.
Geographical segments can be based on location of production/assets or location of customers.

flow.title: Identifying Segment Type
steps: Evaluate risks and returns of operations
Check product nature and production similarity
Check location of assets or location of customers
Group related units into Business or Geographical Segments

topics.example: A firm selling automobile batteries vs UPS batteries has two business segments due to different risk factors.
remember: Business segments group products with similar risk profile.
Geographical segments can exist even within a single country if economic environments differ.
mistakes: Assuming geographical segments can only be divided by national international borders.

quiz.q: Which factor is considered when identifying a Business Segment?
quiz.why: Nature of production processes is a factor used to determine business segments.

quiz.q: Geographical segments can be based on which of the following?
o: Location of facilities or location of customers
Tax rates applied to head office
quiz.why: AS 17 allows geographical segments based on either asset location or customer location.

topics.title: Segment Revenue, Expense, Result, Assets & Liabilities
explain: Segment Revenue includes direct external revenue, allocable revenue, and inter-segment sales.
Segment Expense includes direct operating expenses, allocable expenses, and inter-segment expenses.
Segment Result is calculated as Segment Revenue minus Segment Expense.
Segment Assets and Liabilities exclude income tax assets/liabilities and general head-office items.
Interest expense is excluded from segment expense unless segment operations are financial in nature or capitalized under AS 16.

flow.title: Calculating Segment Result
steps: Aggregate external and inter-segment revenues
Deduct direct and allocable operating expenses
Exclude tax, head-office costs, and financing interest
Obtain final Segment Result

topics.example: Allocating ₹5,00,000 direct sales and ₹1,00,000 internal transfers while excluding ₹50,000 income tax asset to compute segment figures.
remember: Segment Assets exclude Income Tax assets (including Deferred Tax Assets).
Segment Liabilities exclude borrowings incurred for financing purposes.
mistakes: Including deferred tax assets or income tax liabilities in segment assets or liabilities.

quiz.q: Which item is EXCLUDED from Segment Revenue?
quiz.why: Segment revenue explicitly excludes extraordinary items as defined in AS 5.

quiz.q: What must be deducted from gross assets when evaluating Segment Assets?
o: Income tax assets and head-office assets
quiz.why: Segment assets do not include income tax assets and head-office assets.

topics.title: Identifying Reportable Segments (Quantitative Thresholds)
explain: Revenue Test: Total revenue (external + internal) is 10% or more of total revenue of all segments.
Profit/Loss Test: Absolute profit/loss is 10% or more of greater of total profit of profitable segments or total loss of loss-making segments.
Asset Test: Segment assets are 10% or more of total assets of all segments.
Overall 75% Test: Total external revenue of reportable segments must equal at least 75% of total enterprise external revenue.
If a segment was reportable in the preceding period, it continues to be reportable in the current period.

flow.title: Reportable Segment Identification Process
steps: Apply 10% Revenue Test
Apply 10% Profit/Loss Test
Apply 10% Asset Test
If any 10% test passes, segment is Reportable
Verify if total external revenue of reportable segments >= 75%
Add non-reportable segments if 75% target is not met

topics.example: If Segment A has ₹225 lakhs profit and max benchmark is ₹300 lakhs (10% = ₹30 lakhs), Segment A passes the profit test.
remember: Passing ANY ONE 10% test makes a segment reportable.
75% overall test considers ONLY external revenue.
mistakes: Using net profit (profits minus losses) instead of higher of total profit or total loss for the 10% benchmark.

quiz.q: A segment is reportable if its total revenue is at least what percentage of total segment revenue?
quiz.why: The quantitative materiality threshold for revenue is 10% or more.

quiz.q: The overall 75% test for reportable segments considers which type of revenue?
o: Total of external and internal revenue
quiz.why: The overall 75% threshold test requires that external revenue of reportable segments constitutes at least 75% of total enterprise external revenue.

topics.title: Primary & Secondary Segment Reporting Formats
explain: Primary format depends on whether enterprise risks/returns are driven by products (business) or locations (geographical).
Primary segment disclosures require segment revenue, result, assets, liabilities, capital expenditure, and depreciation.
Secondary segment disclosures require external revenue, carrying assets, and capital expenditure for secondary segments exceeding 10% thresholds.
Inter-segment transfers must be disclosed using the actual transfer pricing basis used by the enterprise.

flow.title: Determining Primary vs Secondary Format
steps: Identify predominant source of risks and returns
Set primary format (Business or Geographical)
Set secondary format as the remaining type
Disclose full primary details and concise secondary details

topics.example: A company charging inter-segment sales at cost less 10% discloses this actual pricing policy in its financial notes.
remember: Primary format requires detailed reporting including result and liabilities.
Transfer pricing policy must be disclosed and applied consistently.
mistakes: Forcing market pricing on inter-segment transfers when company actually used cost-based pricing.

quiz.q: What determines whether business or geographical segments form the primary reporting format?
o: Dominant source and nature of risks and returns
Number of employees in each segment
Total tax paid in domestic market
quiz.why: The dominant source and nature of risks and returns govern the primary segment reporting format.

quiz.q: How should inter-segment transfers be priced for AS 17 reporting?
o: On the basis actually used by enterprise to price transfers
quiz.why: AS 17 requires inter-segment transfers to be measured on the basis that the enterprise actually used to price them.

topics.title: Practical Calculations & Special Case Scenarios
explain: To test asset threshold, deduct deferred tax assets from total segment assets first.
To test profitability threshold, sum all segment profits separately and all segment losses separately, then take 10% of the larger total.
Unallocated corporate assets (like head office assets) are added back during reconciliation to reach total enterprise assets.
Any segment designated by management can be reportable regardless of quantitative thresholds.

flow.title: Asset Test Calculation Flow
steps: Take total reported assets of each segment
Subtract deferred tax and income tax assets
Calculate revised total enterprise assets
Compute 10% threshold of revised total
Compare each segment asset against 10% threshold

topics.example: Total assets = ₹10 crores. Deferred tax assets = ₹1.2 crores. Revised total assets = ₹8.8 crores. Threshold = ₹0.88 crores.
remember: Always adjust total assets by removing tax assets before running 10% asset test.
Head office expenses and interest expenses are reconciled below Segment Result.
mistakes: Including head office costs in segment operating expenses without a reasonable allocation basis.

quiz.q: If Segment P has assets of ₹4 crores including ₹1 crore deferred tax assets, what are its segment assets under AS 17?
quiz.why: Deferred tax assets are excluded from segment assets (₹4 - ₹1 = ₹3 crores).

quiz.q: Profitable segments total profit is ₹8,280 crores and loss-making segments total loss is ₹6,800 crores. What is the benchmark amount for 10% profit/loss test?
quiz.why: The benchmark is the greater absolute figure between total profits (₹8,280 cr) and total losses (₹6,800 cr).
